correctness.rationale: For v_N=u_N+z/√N, the sum of third absolute moments of the scaled centered Bernoulli summands is O(N⁻¹ᐟ²): their failure probabilities exponentially suppress the large normalized weights. The scaled sum has variance tending to V>0, and √N times its mean excess over θ tends to zD, by local uniform convergence of the differentiated mean sums. The exact strict-crossing event is that the weight exceeds θ at v_N; normal continuity justifies the inversion without excluding finite ties. For the displacement, use the undiscovered mass, not a Riemann-sum error estimate on the singular discovered-mass integrand. The undiscovered-mass integrand extends smoothly at zero, with uniform O(N⁻¹) error near the root, smaller than N^(s−1). Its integral has c-derivative (1−θ−uD)/b at c=b. With c_N−b=−b²ζ(s)N^(s−1)+o(N^(s−1)), the sign and constant of the stated inverse displacement follow. Adding this shift to the tight finite-root fluctuation gives exactly the stated cases, including the condition δ≠0 on supercritical divergence.
residual_risks: Parameters are fixed. The frozen theorem does not resolve continuum centering at a zero leading coefficient when s>1/2. The finite numerical checks are not proof or formal verification.
